findings.title: Applet highscore and level traffic uses unauthenticated HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
URL connection				= new URL( fileName );
data						= new DataInputStream( connection.openStream() );
findings.entry_point: ApoStarzApplet.init() at apoStarz/ApoStarzApplet.java:24-33. Its super.init() sets ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true at org/apogames/ApoApplet.java:34-39.
findings.sink: URL.openStream() at org/apogames/ApoIO.java:220-221 for the binary highscore, URL.openStream() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzIO.java:102-103 for text levels, and HttpURLConnection.getOutputStream() at org/apogames/ApoIO.java:166-169 for highscore uploads.
findings.data_path: ApoStarzGame.APPLET_LEVEL is the literal http://apo-games.de/apoStarz/levels/ at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:36. Game.init() appends highscore.hig and calls ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel() at lines 144-147, which reaches ApoIO.readLevel() and openStream(). setNormalMode() at lines 432-435 and ApoStarzTutorial.init() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzTutorial.java:43-46 pass HTTP .ase URLs through ApoStarzGame.levelLoad(), ApoStarzIO.readLevel(), and its openStream(). The win path at ApoStarzGame.java:591-597 sends the binary highscore back through ApoIO.writeLevel().
findings.attack_scenario: A player launches the legacy applet. A network attacker intercepts the plain-HTTP request for highscore.hig or an .ase file and returns a syntactically valid replacement containing attacker-selected scores, solutions, or level strings. The game consumes it without transport authentication, allowing leaderboard/content manipulation or a parser denial of service. The attacker can likewise observe or alter the cleartext highscore request body sent after a win.
findings.preconditions: The JApplet entry point must be run in a legacy applet-capable environment, and the attacker must control apo-games.de or the network path to it. The desktop ApoStarzMain path is not affected because ApoConstants.B_APPLET defaults to false at org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:13.
findings.validation_plan: Run ApoStarzApplet through an intercepting HTTP proxy or map apo-games.de to a controlled HTTP server. Serve a valid highscore.hig with a visibly altered score and a valid .ase file with a visibly altered level. Confirm requests are HTTP, not HTTPS, and confirm the altered values appear in the game. Complete a level and capture the cleartext request generated by ApoStarzGame.java:597 and ApoIO.java:166-174.

findings.title: Four-character .ase level triggers a non-terminating parser loop
findings.entry_point: A user-selected .ase file reaches ApoStarzGame.levelLoad() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:533-548 or ApoStarzEditor.levelLoad() at apoStarz/editor/ApoStarzEditor.java:306-314. In applet mode, HTTP-delivered level files reach the same path from ApoStarzGame.java:432-435 and ApoStarzTutorial.java:43-46.
findings.sink: The coordinate-normalization loop at ApoStarzLevelLoad.java:209-211, whose decrement becomes zero when the parsed level width is 2.
findings.data_path: ApoStarzIO.readLevel() reads each attacker-controlled line into allLevels at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzIO.java:95-108. ApoStarzGame.setLevelString() passes it to ApoStarzLevel.loadLevel() at ApoStarzGame.java:501-503 and ApoStarzLevel.java:243-245. ApoStarzLevelLoad.loadLevel() selects method one from the first character at lines 24-34; setWidth() converts the second character with width = c - 96 at lines 151-159; setWall() then enters the loop at lines 190-214.
findings.attack_scenario: Create an .ase file whose first line is exactly ab"!. The first a selects method one, b produces width 2, the double quote declares one wall, and ! decodes to position 1. At line 209 the condition becomes 1 > 0, while line 211 repeatedly subtracts 0. Opening the file freezes the game thread and consumes a CPU core. A malicious level/highscore server can deliver the same level string to the applet.
findings.preconditions: The victim must open the crafted .ase file, use a user-editable fixed level file, or run applet mode against a malicious/intercepted level or highscore response.
findings.validation_plan: Put the single line ab"! in a file named hang.ase, launch the desktop game, choose Load, and select it. Run the process under a timeout and capture a thread dump. Continuous CPU use and a stack fixed at ApoStarzLevelLoad.setWall(), lines 209-211, confirm the issue.

findings.title: Zero-record highscore file crashes game initialization
findings.entry_point: The automatically loaded user.dir/levels/highscore.hig at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:144-150, or the applet's HTTP highscore response at line 147.
findings.sink: ArrayList.get(0) on an empty levels list at ApoStarzHighscore.java:104.
findings.data_path: ApoStarzGame.init() calls ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel(); org/apogames/ApoIO.java:209-224 opens the local file or URL and dispatches to ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel(). A four-byte zero count is accepted at ApoStarzHighscore.java:139-146 and leaves levels empty. Game.init() then calls setMenuMode() at ApoStarzGame.java:403, which calls getRandomLevel() at line 448 and reaches the unchecked get() sink.
findings.attack_scenario: A local attacker replaces levels/highscore.hig with four zero bytes, or a malicious server/network attacker returns those bytes to the applet. On the next launch, the parser accepts a record count of zero. Menu initialization immediately requests a random level and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, preventing normal startup.
findings.preconditions: The attacker needs write access to the game's working-directory levels/highscore.hig file, or control of the applet's HTTP response.
findings.validation_plan: Back up highscore.hig, replace it with bytes 00 00 00 00, and launch ApoStarzMain from the directory containing levels. Confirm initialization terminates with IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoStarzHighscore.getRandomLevel() line 104. Repeat in applet mode by serving the same four-byte response.

findings.title: Writable local highscore records have no integrity check
findings.entry_point: The fixed user-editable file user.dir/levels/highscore.hig loaded by ApoStarzGame.init() at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:144-150.
findings.sink: The unverified score and solution are installed as authoritative ApoStarzHighscoreLevel values at ApoStarzHighscore.java:143-146. They are retrieved at lines 120-135 and displayed by ApoStarzGame.renderSteps() at ApoStarzGame.java:1060-1063.
findings.data_path: ApoStarzGame.init() passes the fixed path to ApoIO.readLevel(); ApoIO.java:215-224 reads the bytes directly; ApoStarzHighscore.readLevel() accepts the count, level string, score, and solution at lines 139-146 without a signature, keyed MAC, or other provenance check. ApoStarzGame.setLevelString() copies these values into curHighscore and levelSolution at lines 527-529.
findings.attack_scenario: A local player copies a valid level code from an .ase file and constructs highscore.hig with one DataOutputStream record containing that code, an artificial score such as 1, and a non-empty solution. On launch, the game accepts and displays the fabricated record as its highscore. This affects only the local game; the source does not establish that the desktop value reaches a shared server.
findings.preconditions: The player must be able to edit user.dir/levels/highscore.hig and must encode strings using DataOutputStream.writeUTF so the custom parser accepts them.
findings.validation_plan: Use a small Java helper with DataOutputStream to write: int 1, writeUTF(valid level code), int 1, and writeUTF("r"). Place the result at levels/highscore.hig, launch the desktop game, select the matching level, and confirm Highscore: 1 and the injected solution are shown.

findings.title: Dormant URL class loader can instantiate unsigned classes
findings.entry_point: No shipped entry point. A repository-wide reference search found no construction or invocation outside ApoClassLoader.java itself.
findings.sink: URLClassLoader.loadClass() followed by Class.newInstance() at ApoClassLoader.java:69-75, which can initialize and construct code obtained from the configured URL.
findings.data_path: A hypothetical caller supplies path and classname to the public constructor at ApoClassLoader.java:19-22 or setters at lines 36-38 and 52-54, sets applet mode so path is interpreted as a URL at lines 65-68, and calls getMyClass() at line 62.
findings.attack_scenario: There is no attack path through the shipped ApoStarz UI, main method, applet, file formats, or network responses. If future integration passes an attacker-controlled URL and class name to this utility and invokes getMyClass(), the attacker can host a class whose static initializer or constructor executes with the game's process privileges.
findings.preconditions: Additional code must call the otherwise-unused utility with attacker-controlled arguments, and the Java runtime policy must permit URL class loading. These conditions are not present in this variant.
findings.validation_plan: First confirm the absence of callers with a full-source search for new ApoClassLoader and getMyClass. To demonstrate only the dormant capability, create a separate harness that sets ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true, hosts a test class over HTTP, invokes new ApoClassLoader(baseUrl, className).getMyClass(), and observes a constructor-created marker. This does not demonstrate reachability in the shipped game.

notes: All 49 Java files in the snapshot were opened. The desktop entry ignores command-line arguments at apoStarz/ApoStarzMain.java:52-53; network loading is gated by applet mode, whose flag defaults false at org/apogames/ApoConstants.java:13 and is set by org/apogames/ApoApplet.java:34-39. The concrete formats are text .ase files named at apoStarz/ApoStarzConstants.java:47 and binary highscore.hig loaded at apoStarz/game/ApoStarzGame.java:147-149. The full review found no ObjectInputStream/readObject, MessageDigest, JNI/System.load, or .cheat, .mar, .skunk, .defence, or .rep references. ApoClassLoader uses URLClassLoader rather than defineClass and is intentionally reported as theoretical because it has no caller.
